import pypdf
from pypdf import PdfReader, PdfWriter
r = PdfReader('permit-form.pdf')
w = PdfWriter()
w.append(r)
# fill fields
data = {
    'organizer': 'Tidewater Studio',
    'event_date': '2026-12-05',
    'location': 'North Cove Lawn',
    'attendees': 'about 40',
}
w.update_page_form_field_values(w.pages[0], data, auto_regenerate=False)
# flatten: merge form fields into page content so they can't be edited
# pypdf doesn't flatten directly; use a manual approach: set NeedAppearances false and remove AcroForm interactivity
# Simplest robust flatten: render each page to image? No - we want vector. Use pypdf's set_need_appearances and then remove the AcroForm.
w.set_need_appearances_writer(False)
# Remove the AcroForm so fields are no longer interactive (flattened visually via appearance streams already generated)
if '/AcroForm' in w._root_object:
    del w._root_object['/AcroForm']
with open('out/permit-filled.pdf','wb') as f:
    w.write(f)
print('written')
# verify

print('fields after:', r2.get_fields())
print('text:', r2.pages[0].extract_text())
